intro: {n} quick statements about life on the road. Rate each one from Not me at all to Totally me, and the Pokédex does the rest.
hint: About two minutes · 200 possible results · no sign-up

q.e1: After a long day of training, you'd rather celebrate at a packed Pokémon Center than rest alone.
q.e2: You're the trainer who starts the chant in the stadium crowd.
q.e3: On a new route, you talk to every trainer you pass, not just the ones who challenge you.
q.e4: You'd happily spend a week in a quiet cave with a good book and one Pokémon.
q.e5: At a big town festival, you drift to the edge of the crowd and watch.
q.e6: Long conversations with strangers at the Pokémon Center drain you.
q.a1: You'd give your last Potion to a rival's injured Pokémon without thinking twice.
q.a2: When a wild Pokémon is cornered, your first instinct is to calm it, not catch it.
q.a3: You'd stop mid-journey to help a lost kid find their Pokémon, badge deadline or not.
q.a4: If a trainer blocks the bridge, you push past rather than wait your turn.
q.a5: You keep score of favours, and you expect them returned.
q.a6: Teasing a nervous trainer before a battle feels like fair game to you.
q.c1: Your bag is sorted: Potions in one pocket, Poké Balls in another, badges polished.
q.c2: You plan the whole route through Victory Road before taking a single step.
q.c3: You train every single day, even when nobody is watching.
q.c4: You've walked into a Gym with no idea what type the leader uses.
q.c5: Your Pokémon's held items are whatever happened to be in your bag.
q.c6: Gym schedules, ferry times, league deadlines: close enough is good enough.
q.o1: A strange ruin with glowing symbols? You're inside before anyone can stop you.
q.o2: You'd rather learn a weird new move than master an old reliable one.
q.o3: You've genuinely wondered what the Unown are trying to say.
q.o4: You like the Pokémon you've always liked; new regions can keep their novelties.
q.o5: You've used the same team for years and see no reason to change it.
q.o6: Legends, dreams, mysteries: you'd rather deal with what's in front of you.
q.s1: When your last Pokémon is at 1 HP, your hands stay steady.
q.s2: A loss at the Pokémon League stings for an afternoon, then it's gone.
q.s3: Storms, Ghost-types, dark forests: you're hard to rattle.
q.s4: One critical hit against you can ruin your whole day.
q.s5: Before a Gym battle, your stomach is in knots.
q.s6: You replay a lost battle in your head for days.
q.k1: You've reset a run because your starter's nature wasn't perfect.
q.k2: Being the very best, like no one ever was, is a real goal for you, not a song.
q.k3: A friendly battle still has a winner, and it had better be you.
q.k4: You'd rather raise a happy team than a strong one.
q.k5: Contests, battles, races: you join for the fun and forget who won.
q.k6: When a rival wants a rematch, you'd honestly rather go get lunch.
q.i1: You'd set out on your journey alone before you'd wait around for a travel companion.
q.i2: You'd leave a trainer who holds you back, even one you like.
q.i3: You make your own rules on the road; a Gym Leader's advice is optional.
q.i4: You'd give up a badge before you'd leave a friend behind.
q.i5: You stay with the same travel companions for the whole journey.
q.i6: One trainer, for life: that's the only kind of bond you'd want.
